Write registry attributes to a user-defined dictionary

Source: R/write_registry.R
write_registry.Rd

Compatibility interface for cr_map(), using dict instead of attr. New grouping workflows can use cr_map() directly.

Usage

write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Default S3 method
write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'list'
write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class '`NULL`'
write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'character'
write_registry(
  x = NULL,
  dict = "registry",
  cache_refresh = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A named list, a named character vector or a data frame that includes the columns regicode and the target attribute e.g., registry, area_type.

dict

A character string specifying the dictionary to update. Built-in defaults are available for "registry" and "area_type"; any other name is treated as a user-defined dictionary name. The name regicode is reserved for write_regicode().

cache_refresh

If TRUE, refresh the dictionary to default values before updating. User-supplied mappings are then applied on top of those defaults.

quiet

If TRUE, suppresses update and backup messages and returns the updated dictionary invisibly.

Value

A tibble with two columns: regicode and the corresponding attribute values. The result is returned invisibly when quiet = TRUE.

Details

Stores mappings from registry identifiers to their attributes, e.g., China-specific registry names or area types, in a dictionary file. This supports consistent labeling and downstream processing in cancer registry data.

This function allows users to build or update local mapping dictionaries for registry-level attributes. It supports multiple input formats and updates files saved in the user-specific R configuration directory. Registry identifiers must be non-empty and unique within one update. Set options(canregtools.dict_dir = "path/to/dictionaries") to isolate dictionaries for a project. By default the user configuration directory is used. Only user overrides are stored; current built-in defaults are merged when reading. Legacy dictionaries are backed up and migrated on their next update, retaining all legacy entries as overrides because their origin is unknown. Corrupt files stop the update and are retained. Writes use a verified temporary file and replacement, with a lock against concurrent writers. Use reset_dict() to clear overrides (with a backup). cache_refresh = TRUE retains its reset-before-update behavior.

Examples

withr::with_options(
  list(canregtools.dict_dir = tempfile("canregtools-example-")),
  write_registry(list("410302" = "410301"))
)

# Registry attributes stored in data frame
registry_dict <- data.frame(
regicode = c("410302", "410303", "410304", "410305", "410306", "410307"),
registry = c(rep("410301", 5), "410300"),
area_type = rep("urban", 6)
)
withr::with_options(
  list(canregtools.dict_dir = tempfile("canregtools-example-")),
  write_registry(registry_dict)
)

# Registry attributes stored in list
dict <- list(
'410302' = '410301',
'410303' = '410301',
'410304' = '410301',
'410305' = '410301',
'410306' = '410301',
'410307' = '410301'
)
withr::with_options(
  list(canregtools.dict_dir = tempfile("canregtools-example-")),
  write_registry(dict)
)

# Registry attributes using built-in information
dict <- NULL
withr::with_options(
  list(canregtools.dict_dir = tempfile("canregtools-example-")),
  write_registry(dict)
)

# Registry attributes stored in named character vector with regicode as
# name and attributes as values
dict <- rep("410301", 5)
names(dict) <- c("410302", "410303", "410304", "410305", "410306")
withr::with_options(
  list(canregtools.dict_dir = tempfile("canregtools-example-")),
  write_registry(dict)
)
